source: Grierson1906 Linguistic Survey of India volume IV

evidence.finding: General key represents nasalization by a tilde above the affected letter and uses raised small vowels for weakly pronounced vowels.
General key explicitly uses an apostrophe for Munda semi-consonants (k, t, p examples). An apostrophe is not intrinsically an unresolved transcription or exclusion.
Santali pronunciation discussion warns that long vowels are inconsistently marked across witnesses; do not insert or remove length marks by analogy.

Santali key distinguishes open and closed vowel qualities, nasal vowels, and underdotted neutral vowels. Stacked marks in related specimens must not be reduced to plain macrons. Exact combining order remains a separate literal-reading task.

Mundari pronunciation discussion explicitly says Bodding Birbhum Koda material informed preparation of the Mundari standard list, while received specimens were retained with limited changes. This does not make the published Mundari table a separately labelled Birbhum table; retain published attribution.
Birbhum pronunciation is explicitly cross-referenced to Mundari; Bodding is credited for the specimen.

policy: Preserve literal vowel quality, length, nasalization, underdots, apostrophes and source word boundaries. Do not infer IPA or replace unclear text by cognates. Conventions alone do not resolve damaged individual glyphs.

alternate_scan_check.finding: Archive source dimensions equal local DjVu dimensions, so no larger archive download is justified as a resolution improvement.
